newsitem.title: Hong Kong: Blair eager build strong relationship with China.
newsitem.headline: Blair eager build strong relationship with China.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Monday he was eager to build a strong and stable relationship with China but added that Beijing must keep to its promises on Hong Kong's freedoms.
Blair flew into Hong Kong on a rain-swept morning to attend Monday's midnight ceremony that marks the end of 156 years of colonial rule in Hong Kong, which is being returned to China.
Before attending the handover, Blair and Foreign Secretary Robin Cook will meet China's President Jiang Zemin for one hour of talks at a harbour-front hotel.
Asked what message he would deliver, Blair told reporters: "What is absolutely essential is that there are two pillars, foundations of our relationship for the future.
"The first is adherence to the Joint Declaration, the agreement between Britain and China that guarantees the future prosperity and freedom of Hong Kong.

"Second is our desire to build a strong and stable relationship with China for the future which is both in the interest of the people of Hong Kong as well as the people of the United Kingdom," he said.

China is disbanding Hong Kong's elected legislature and rolling back some key political freedoms in Hong Kong to reverse political reforms it says were introduced without its consent in the twilight years of British rule.

Beijing, which sees the handover putting an end to a century and a half of humiliation, plans to install an appointed Provisional Legislature early on Tuesday morning until new elections are held next year.
Blair, who together with Cook is to boycott the swearing in of the new Provisional Legislature, kept stressing to reporters what would underpin Sino-British relations in future.
"The absolute basic foundation has got to be adherence to the Joint Declaration," Blair said after being greeted at Kai Tak airport by Britain's 28th and final governor, Chris Patten.

The watering down of Hong Kong's civil rights and democracy is fiercely opposed by Britain and by Hong Kong's own democracy movement, which won 70 percent of the directly elected seats in legislative elections in 1995.
Blair, underlining the historic nature of his brief visit, said: "This is obviously a momentous day for China, for Britain and most of all the people of Hong Kong.
"Hong Kong has become one of the most successful and prosperous parts of the world."
